features.name: Project skeleton and tooling
features.behavior: Laravel application in web/ with Vue 3 + TypeScript via Inertia, Pest, Larastan, Pint, ESLint, vue-tsc and Vitest; Docker Compose with PostgreSQL, Redis and Mailpit; tools/ launchers wire PHP and Node tooling into the harness lint, typecheck, test and build scripts.
features.verification: A health route returns 200 in a Pest test; npm run lint, typecheck, test and build run the PHP and front-end tools and pass; docker compose up serves the app.

features.name: Tenancy foundation
features.behavior: Tenant model, tenant resolution from the request subdomain, a BelongsToTenant trait with a global scope and automatic tenant_id on create, tenant context carried into queued jobs, and a test helper that creates two tenants.
features.verification: Tests prove a record created in tenant A is invisible to tenant B in queries, routes and queued jobs; an architecture test fails if a tenant-owned model lacks the trait or bypasses the scope.

features.name: Authentication and roles
features.behavior: Users belong to a tenant (the same email may exist in two tenants), login and registration, roles owner, staff and customer, and Laravel policies enforcing them.
features.verification: Tests cover every role and a user from another tenant for each protected action; a user cannot sign in to a different tenant.

features.name: Bookings with capacity locking
features.behavior: Booking a session inside a transaction with a row lock, so capacity is never exceeded; a customer cannot double-book the same session.
features.verification: A concurrency test fires parallel booking requests at the last spot and asserts exactly one succeeds and capacity is never exceeded.

features.name: Stripe webhooks and payment failures
features.behavior: Signature-verified, idempotent webhook handling with stored event ids, a grace period after a failed payment, and suspension of booking rights.
features.verification: Replaying the same webhook twice changes state once; failed-payment fixtures move a customer through grace to suspended; a bad signature is rejected.
